## Project Idea

We will be participating in the NYC Open Data project gallery. The main objective of our project will be developing a website that shows an interactive map of NYC that allows users to see where 311 service requests occur. This would allow a user to answer questions like: "which borough had the most rat infestation 311 complaints in 2020 - 2025?" The dataset we will be using ([found here](https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Social-Services/311-Service-Requests-from-2020-to-Present/erm2-nwe9/about_data)) contains 23 million rows where each row represents an individual 311 service request with corresponding information. The fields which will be most important to the development of our project are:

- **create_date** - in order to track complaints over time

- **complaint_type** and **descriptor** - information about the nature of the 311 complaint

- **location type** - filtering by residential building or sidewalk, etc.

- **incident_zip**, **incident_address**, **city**, **borough**, **location** - geographic data which can be used to build the map

## Initial Analysis

For the initial analysis below I will be using the nycOpenData library, which uses their api to import the data. Without an API key though, it restricts the size of import to 10,000 records, so the initial analysis will be done using that.

### Importing Libraries and Data

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(nycOpenData)
library(ggplot2)
library(sf)
library(leaflet)

sample_311 = nyc_any_dataset('https://data.cityofnewyork.us/resource/erm2-nwe9.json') 
```

### Most common complaints

The most common types of complaints (in the sample) seem to be illegal parking, heat/hot water, noise, and then unsanitary conditions

```{r}
complaints = sample_311 |> count(complaint_type, sort = TRUE) # Types of complaints that can show up across

complaints

complaints |> 
  head(10) |>
  ggplot(aes(y = fct_rev(fct_infreq(complaint_type, n)), x = n)) +
  geom_col(color = "white", fill = "lightblue") +
  labs(
    title = "Most Frequent 311 Complaint Types",
    x = "Count",
    y = "311 Complaint Type",
    caption = "Disclaimer: 10,000 row sample"
  )
```

### Map of pest complaints

```{r}
pest_data = sample_311 |>
  filter(
    complaint_type == "UNSANITARY CONDITION" &
    descriptor == "PESTS"
  )

pal = colorFactor(palette = "Set1",
                  domain = pest_data$park_borough)
```

```{r}
leaflet(data = pest_data) %>%
  addTiles() %>%
  addCircleMarkers(
    lng = ~longitude,
    lat = ~latitude,
    fillColor = ~pal(park_borough),
    color = ~pal(park_borough), # Colors the outer ring to match (or set stroke = FALSE)
  )
```
